summary: Defines the Management Information Base objects used to manage version 2 of the OSPF routing protocol, which works with IPv4. OSPF version 3 is handled separately.

eli5.summary: OSPF is how routers tell each other the best roads for data. This note lists the gauges and switches that let a manager look at and adjust a router's OSPF settings.

questions: how to monitor ospf with snmp
how do i enable ospf with snmp
subtitle: The SNMP objects and traps that let a network manager inspect and configure OSPF version 2 on a router.

tldr.problem: OSPF version 2 has many features and settings, and operators need a standard way to read and change them on routers from different vendors.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the OSPF-MIB module (rooted at mib-2 14), a set of tables and variables for areas, interfaces, neighbors and the link state database, plus an optional OSPF-TRAP-MIB module of notifications.
tldr.outcome: It obsoletes RFC 1850 while staying backwards compatible, and adds support for NSSAs, Opaque LSAs, graceful restart and stub routers. OSPF version 3 is not covered.

today: RFC 4750 is a Proposed Standard and obsoletes RFC 1850. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Overview and Management Framework
sections.content:
This memo defines part of the Management Information Base (MIB) for managing version 2 of the Open Shortest Path First routing protocol. OSPF version 2 is specific to IPv4; version 3 is specific to IPv6 and is not what this document manages.

MIB objects are generally accessed through the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) and are written in the Structure of Management Information, here SMIv2. The MIB supports the base OSPFv2 specification in RFC 2328 and extensions such as database overflow, demand circuits, Opaque LSAs, NSSAs and graceful restart.

The document obsoletes RFC 1850 but is designed to be backwards compatible. Appendix B lists the functional differences.
sections.eli5: A router keeps lots of notes about how it is finding roads. This document says what each note is called, so any manager can read them the same way on any router.

sections.title: Structure of the MIB
sections.content:
The MIB is split into sections: general variables, the area data structure, the area stub metric table, the link state database, the address range table, the host table, the interface and interface metric tables, the virtual interface table, the neighbor and virtual neighbor tables, the external link state database, the aggregate range table, the local link state database and the AS-scope link state database.

The general variables are global to the OSPF process. The area table lists every OSPF area the router takes part in, including data for Not-So-Stubby-Area (NSSA) translation. The link state database tables exist mainly to give detailed information for network debugging.

Interface and neighbor tables describe the IP interfaces given to OSPF and the neighbors found on them. Virtual links get parallel tables. The local and AS-scope link state database tables have the same format as the main one but hold only link-local (Opaque type-9) or AS-scoped advertisements. A separate area LSA count table keeps the number of advertisements per area and per LSA type.
sections.eli5: It is like a filing cabinet with one drawer for the whole router, one for each neighborhood it belongs to, one for each of its connections, and one for each router next door.

sections.title: Defaults, Row Creation and Counters
sections.content:
Because OSPF is complex, the MIB defines default values for virtually every object. With IP and the ifTable already configured, the simplest setup is a single SET: ospfAdminStat := enabled. The router ID is then one of the device's IP addresses, every IP interface becomes an OSPF interface in area 0.0.0.0 (the backbone), and authentication is disabled.

The default timers are a Hello Interval of 10 seconds, a Dead Timeout of 40 seconds, a Retransmission interval of 5 seconds, a Transit Delay of 1 second and a Poll Interval of 120 seconds. Non-broadcast multi-access (NBMA) interfaces need at least one configured neighbor.

For creating table rows, DEFVAL clauses suggest values for anything a Set-Request leaves out. Management stations should include as many columns as possible, while agents should accept requests with as few as they need.

The MIB defines several counters, such as ospfSpfRuns and ospfIfEvents. Managers should read ospfDiscontinuityTime to learn whether an event, for example a restart of the OSPF process, has invalidated their view of the counters. SNMPv3 contexts can be used to give views onto multiple OSPF instances on one system.
sections.eli5: The gauges come set to sensible starting positions, so you flip one switch to turn OSPF on. There is also a clock that tells you if the counters were reset, so you do not trust old numbers.

sections.title: Textual Conventions in the Module
sections.content:
The module starts with a handful of textual conventions that give OSPF values their shape. AreaID and RouterID have the format of an IP address; an Area ID defines a summarization point, while a Router ID identifies the router independently of its IP address.

Metric is an integer from 0 to FFFF hex and BigMetric, the external metric, runs from 0 to FFFFFF hex. HelloRange covers 1 to FFFF seconds, UpToMaxAge covers 0 to 3600 seconds, and DesignatedRouterPriority covers 0 to FF hex. Status is simply enabled (1) or disabled (2).
sections.eli5: These are the rules for what kind of number or label each setting can hold, like saying a dial only goes from 0 to 10.

sections.title: OSPF Traps
sections.content:
OSPF is event-driven, and finding the source of a topology change by polling many routers is hard. The optional OSPF trap module (OSPF-TRAP-MIB, rooted at {ospf 16}) lets a router notify the management station of important events. Each notification carries the originator's Router ID.

To limit trap volume the RFC suggests four mechanisms. A router should not originate expected interface-related traps until two dead-timer intervals have passed after OSPF starts. All trap types except ospfLsdbOverflow and ospfLsdbApproachingOverflow share one sliding window that bounds the number of traps; appropriate values are 7 traps in a window of 10 seconds. OSPF should generate at most one trap per OSPF event. Managers can poll event counters and enable specific traps only when a counter rises abnormally.

Since the original modules were written for SNMPv1, the RFC explains how notifications translate between SNMP versions using RFC 3584, and notes that the translation is not reversible.
sections.eli5: Traps are alarm bells. To stop them from ringing nonstop when a router first wakes up, there are rules to wait a bit and to limit how many can ring at once.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Objects with read-write or read-create access can be sensitive. Using SET operations without proper protection can hurt network operations. Special attention is called for on ospfIfAuthKey, ospfIfAuthType, ospfVirtIfAuthKey and ospfVirtIfAuthType. Where SNMPv3 strong security (authentication and encryption) is not used, these objects should be read-only, not read-create.

SNMPv1 by itself is not a secure environment, even on a network protected by IPsec. The RFC recommends the SNMPv3 User-based Security Model (RFC 3414) and View-based Access Control Model (RFC 3415), and says it is the user's responsibility to configure the SNMP entity so only legitimate principals can read or change the objects.
sections.eli5: These switches can change how a router behaves, so only trusted people should be allowed to touch them, and the passwords for OSPF should not be readable by just anyone.

sections.title: Changes from RFC 1850
sections.content:
Appendix B lists the changes. The general group gained ospfRFC1583Compatibility (default enabled), ospfReferenceBandwidth, graceful restart objects, stub router objects and ospfDiscontinuityTime. The area table gained NSSA translation objects.

Opaque LSA support added the local and virtual local link state database tables and the AS-scope table, with an area-scope (type-10) enumeration. New notifications cover NSSA translator changes and graceful restart status. The external link state database table was deprecated, and authentication objects were reworded because of concerns about cascading security vulnerabilities. Appendix A notes that TOS-specific information is kept only for backward compatibility, since the TOS routing option has been deleted from OSPF.
sections.eli5: This list says what was added to the old version: new gauges for newer OSPF features, and clearer warnings about passwords.
